title: Comparative Analysis of STEM and non-STEM Teachers’ Needs for Integrating AI into Educational Environments
extended_summary:
This paper examines what K-12 teachers need from AI-enhanced educational platforms, especially those used for block-based programming (BBP) and related classroom tasks. The authors focus on three areas: student assessment, course development and resource expansion, and student monitoring/support. The study was motivated by the claim that common BBP platforms such as Code.org, Scratch, and Snap lack AI features that could better support teachers across both STEM and non-STEM subjects.

The study used semi-structured interviews with 8 K-12 teachers from North and South Carolina in the United States, split evenly between STEM and non-STEM disciplines. Participants had prior experience using coding activities in their classrooms, and interviews lasted 40 to 60 minutes. The researchers applied thematic analysis to identify recurring needs and differences between groups. Reported needs included customizable rubrics, more detailed feedback, authenticity/originality checks, AI-supported resource generation, individualized materials, peer-collaboration support, and monitoring tools such as screen control, reminders, and progress tracking.

The main conclusion is that both STEM and non-STEM teachers want AI features that make educational platforms more adaptive, more informative for assessment, and better integrated with classroom workflows. Non-STEM teachers especially emphasized creative and qualitative assessment needs, while STEM teachers more often stressed workflow efficiency and authenticity of student work. The paper argues that future educational platforms should incorporate AI-supported personalization, analytics, and feedback features, while also addressing privacy and school-policy constraints.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative semi-structured interview study with thematic analysis of 8 teachers, so it offers descriptive evidence about needs and perceptions rather than causal effects. It is peer-reviewed and methodologically coherent, but it does not test an intervention or measure outcomes experimentally.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct impact estimate on student or teacher outcomes; it surfaces requirements for future AI-enabled tools. Any impact is indirect and currently unclear, so the evidence supports only a yellow tier.

interventions.use_case: Semi-structured interview study of K-12 teachers' needs for AI-enhanced educational platforms in block-based programming contexts, including assessment, course development, and student monitoring features.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports teacher demand for AI features that would streamline assessment, course development, and monitoring tasks, suggesting perceived gains in teacher workflow efficiency rather than measured learning gains. Across 8 interviewed K-12 teachers (n=8), participants emphasized AI support for rubric customization, detailed feedback, automated content generation, progress tracking, and reducing time spent switching between systems.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes about teacher workload, grading, resource creation, and student monitoring needs

finding.finding_summary: Teachers identified institutional needs around LMS integration, single sign-on, privacy controls, and cross-platform data management for school use of AI-enabled educational tools. In this qualitative sample of 8 K-12 teachers (n=8), the findings indicate that adoption depends on compatibility with school systems and compliance with privacy/security expectations.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes about integration, access control, and privacy/security requirements

finding.finding_summary: A recurring theme was the desire for AI to support collaboration, peer matching, conflict resolution, and creative problem solving in coding and interdisciplinary projects. The study does not quantify effects, but the 8 teacher interviews (n=8) suggest AI-enabled platforms were viewed as potentially helpful for collaboration and creativity in classroom workflows.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes about collaboration, peer feedback, and creativity support

finding.finding_summary: Teachers wanted monitoring and support features such as reminders, pop-up tips, progress alerts, and motivational tools to help students stay on task and persist during assignments. This is a qualitative perception finding from 8 K-12 teacher interviews (n=8), not a measured student outcome, but it indicates expected benefits for engagement and self-regulation.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes about motivation, distraction prevention, reminders, and help prompts
